rubric.meaning: How strongly does the saved evidence justify further focused investigation toward an actionable, material edge?
rubric.disclaimer: A dated editorial research judgment, not a probability of profitability, paper-quality rating, or trading recommendation.

bands.label: Pause
bands.definition: Little supported material advantage, substantial contrary evidence, or no convincing next experiment.

bands.label: Define and test
bands.definition: An interesting mechanism or insight, but substantial evidence gaps. A specific discriminating test could clarify it.

bands.label: Targeted follow-up
bands.definition: A credible, specific pattern warrants more work, but execution, costs, or protected validation remain unresolved.

bands.label: Strong candidate
bands.definition: An economically meaningful effect survives credible separated evaluation under explicit execution and cost assumptions. Remaining confirmation work is bounded.

bands.label: Highest priority
bands.definition: Robust, independently corroborated material evidence supports a clear next controlled validation step.

assessments.scope: Selecting ES 4RXV and NQ 10RXV for reversal follow-through; GC 10RXV is context, not the requested missing GC 20RXV comparison.
assessments.rationale: The development selection failed its declared later checks. Observable follow-through and excursions do not establish an incremental, executable advantage; the missing GC comparison cannot be supplied by another setting.
assessments.materiality: The saved three-bar median adverse/favorable excursions are 9/11 ES ticks and 20/26 NQ ticks. These separate extrema are not a realizable spread or net return; materiality requires net ticks per original opportunity above a fixed same-product comparator.

supporting.text: Held-out ES 4RXV recorded 615/1,985 runs with at least three follow-through bars (31.0%); NQ 10RXV recorded 5,077/15,171 (33.5%). These establish the measured phenomenon, not a trade win rate.

contrary.text: Neither ES nor NQ produced a clear winner under the prespecified validation and held-out significance checks; that primary failure remains a failure.
The requested GC 20RXV evidence was unavailable. Chart completion, source timing and executable fills/costs remain unresolved; chart settings share underlying trades.

assessments.blocker: A failed chart-selection screen and unverified completion/fill timing leave no supported material trading advantage.

nextTest.description: Only reopen one frozen chart-versus-comparator reversal rule on genuinely later, clock-verified completion data, with next-available executable fills, a fixed exit, costs and original opportunities retained.
nextTest.supports: Proposed prospective hurdle: at least one incremental net tick per original opportunity and a date-cluster 95% lower bound above zero, without selecting settings on the evaluation sample.
nextTest.rejects: Reject if later net performance fails that hurdle or the selected chart has no incremental advantage over its frozen comparator.

assessments.scope: Using adverse movement inside the eventually successful follow-through candle to motivate a live reversal entry or stop.
assessments.rationale: The measured candle geometry is useful context, but the cohort is selected by a future successful close. It cannot support a live entry/stop advantage without including failed opportunities and path ordering.
assessments.materiality: Conditioned medians are 3 ES 4RXV ticks and 6 NQ 10RXV ticks; their adverse p90 values are 11 and 25 ticks. Stop risk must be evaluated over all eligible signals, in net ticks after execution costs, rather than these success-conditioned summaries.

supporting.text: Saved successful-candle cohorts contain 12,624 ES 4RXV and 97,350 NQ 10RXV observations, with substantial adverse tails despite successful closes.

contrary.text: The adverse-candle cohort requires the next candle eventually to close in the reversal direction; that future condition is unavailable when entering.
Duration is a raw timestamp proxy and within-bar stop/target ordering, fills and costs were not established. Separate chart sizes are dependent.

assessments.blocker: Future-success selection excludes exactly the failures needed for an actionable stop or entry assessment.

nextTest.description: Freeze a causal reversal signal and one entry/exit/stop policy; replay all original opportunities, including unsuccessful candles, on verified finer paths with executable prices and costs.
nextTest.supports: Support only if the unconditional policy beats a same-product time-matched baseline by at least one net tick per opportunity with a date-cluster 95% lower bound above zero.
nextTest.rejects: Reject if the apparent protection disappears after unsuccessful candles, sequencing and costs enter the denominator.

assessments.scope: Prior larger-chart alignment as a predictor of the next smaller-chart reversal bar; longer-run continuation is not promoted.
assessments.rationale: Strictly earlier larger-chart state has a specific next-bar association. Its weak longer-run lift and absent price-policy evidence justify defining one discriminating test before broader follow-up.
assessments.materiality: The ES 5-to-6 next-bar colour contrast is 3.19 percentage points, not a net return. A material result must produce incremental signed ticks after spread, fees, slippage and waiting relative to otherwise comparable smaller-chart reversals.

supporting.text: ES 5-to-6 held-out aligned versus opposing next-bar colour was 79.34% versus 76.15%, a 3.19-point difference (95% 1.62–4.70). GC 6-to-10 had a smaller positive next-bar contrast.
The larger chart must have completed strictly earlier; equal-second ambiguous alignments are excluded rather than assumed observable.

contrary.text: ES three-bar lift was about 1.02 points with an interval spanning zero, and five-bar lift about 0.14 points with an interval spanning zero; GC longer-run lift also weakened.
Settings share the same price streams. Inferred sessions/completion proxies, missing chart combinations and absent execution/cost modelling limit the association.

assessments.blocker: A colour association has not been converted to incremental net price payoff on genuinely uninspected data.

nextTest.description: Freeze ES 5-to-6 alignment and a single next-completed-bar exit; evaluate later verified completion/tick data against reversals matched on side, run length and clock, using available fills and all costs.
nextTest.supports: Support if incremental after-cost mean is at least one tick per original opportunity and its date-cluster 95% lower bound exceeds zero.
nextTest.rejects: Reject if colour lift survives but net price lift does not, or the effect disappears after matching and causal completion checks.

assessments.scope: The body/close-location/prior-extreme quality stack for aligned reversal continuation, rather than its best bar-colour cell.
assessments.rationale: The quality stack improves some next-bar colour rates while saved signed price returns remain negative. This is substantial contrary evidence to promoting the stack as an entry filter.
assessments.materiality: ES 5-to-6 stacked next-bar mean is about −0.48 ticks versus −0.40 for other aligned reversals, before costs. The 4.63-point colour lift is not an economic gain; materiality requires incremental net ticks under a fixed causal policy.

supporting.text: The ES 5-to-6 stacked cohort had 79.63% next-bar colour continuation versus 75.00%, a 4.63-point difference (95% 2.05–7.14).

contrary.text: ES stacked signed next-bar mean remained negative and was not better than the other aligned cohort; GC 6-to-10 stacked mean was also negative.
Shared chart histories, overlapping quality definitions, completion proxies and absent fills/costs prevent independent or executable-edge claims.

assessments.blocker: The measured colour improvement coexists with negative price payoff; adding an attractive stop after inspection would be a new hypothesis.

assessments.scope: The original first outside-2σ fade and first causal VWAP-touch bounce; later exploratory re-entry and uncomputed plan candidates are separate.
assessments.rationale: The original fade and first-touch bounce show little stable advantage over their declared controls. Later-period uncertainty and reversal under a common tick barrier outweigh frequent VWAP returns.
assessments.materiality: Half-sigma favorable-first rates near 46.8% do not include a complete executable payoff. Materiality is incremental net ticks per original episode versus matched departure/near-approach controls, with missed, neither and ambiguous outcomes retained.

supporting.text: The saved original cohorts contain 86,475 evaluable fade events and 132,202 first-touch events, with both favorable and adverse outcomes retained.
The all-history half-sigma fade contrast versus lesser departures is about +1.11 percentage points, providing limited observational support.

contrary.text: Fade and bounce later-period intervals do not establish stable half-sigma lift. Fixed 8-tick contrasts are negative; the final fade contrast is about −3.16 points and bounce about −2.64 points.
Views share dates, products and anchors, eligibility is retrospective, and fills, costs and overlap are not an execution model. A frequent return is not a trading win rate.

assessments.blocker: The original controls provide weak or contrary incremental evidence, with barrier sensitivity and no protected costed policy validation.

nextTest.description: If reopened, freeze one original candidate, execution/exit rules and a common episode deadline; compare costed policies on later untouched data against the existing matched control, retaining no-trade and unresolved outcomes.
nextTest.supports: Support only if incremental net mean is at least one tick per original episode with a shared-date 95% lower bound above zero and no reversal under the prespecified fixed-tick robustness check.
nextTest.rejects: Reject if lift again vanishes or reverses with comparable barriers, or executable costs eliminate the incremental gain.

assessments.scope: Q1: completed-close persistent versus rotational VWAP state as an incremental predictor of future same-side residence after observable context matching.
assessments.rationale: The specific context-matched residence association is large enough to warrant targeted follow-up. It does not establish a profitable continuation rule, and the study’s other comparisons do not inherit this priority.
assessments.materiality: The matched Q1 contrast is 18.67 percentage points of future residence, not 18.67% return. Materiality requires an executable net-tick advantage above a geometry/clock/volatility-only policy, rather than forecasting residence of a moving reference alone.

supporting.text: Persistent versus rotational Q1 residence retained an 18.67-point contrast (95% 15.53–22.03) after the saved coarse context match.
The primary two-minute state uses completed past closes at fixed landmarks; future observation and warm-up are explicitly separated.

contrary.text: The large raw opposing-slope contrast shrinks to about 2.05 points after context matching; raw state differences can largely reflect geometry.
VWAP predicts the future mean better than TWAP overall, but the last-price baseline has much smaller absolute error. This does not support promoting VWAP as a uniquely superior executable anchor.
All dates were previously inspected; matching is observational and coarse, anchors and sensitivities are dependent, and costs/fills are unresolved.

assessments.blocker: No protected evaluation shows that residual residence information produces a material net price payoff beyond finer distance and clock controls.

nextTest.description: Freeze Q1 state thresholds and a single 30-minute next-available-entry/close-exit policy before new data; test later untouched dates against continuous-distance, clock, volatility and last-price baselines with realistic costs.
nextTest.supports: Support if Q1 adds forecast skill beyond those baselines and at least one incremental net tick per original landmark with a shared-date 95% lower bound above zero.
nextTest.rejects: Reject if the residence lift disappears with finer geometry controls or survives only as moving-reference behaviour without incremental net payoff.

supporting.text: Waiting after exhaustion has favorable point differences versus early entry in ES, NQ and GC, but every familywise interval includes zero.

contrary.text: No primary idea-by-product comparison passes the declared uncertainty and later-block requirements.
Every displayed primary candidate mean is negative after two ticks per executed round trip; wait-policy nontrades correctly remain zero in the original-opportunity denominator.
Older export-clock cohorts and next-bar-start completion proxies remain the executed scope; a later clock correction does not validate fills or rerun quiet-period calibration.

assessments.scope: Waiting for completed C2 confirmation after C1, judged as a price policy over every original C1 opportunity rather than a selected colour subset.
assessments.rationale: Some conditional colour contrasts are positive, but saved waiting price means are negative and waiting loses opportunities. The evidence does not support promoting confirmation as an actionable improvement.
assessments.materiality: The ES 4RXV bearish wait-minus-immediate price contrast is about −0.17 ticks (95% −0.25 to −0.08), before costs. Conditional C3/C4 success must be separated from net ticks per original C1 and the different physical horizons.

supporting.text: Some GC and bearish NQ 10RXV confirmed-colour comparisons pass the ordinary-pair screen; this is limited support for conditional bar behaviour.

contrary.text: Waiting price means are negative throughout the saved chart/side comparison; most wait-minus-immediate means are also negative.
For ES 4RXV bearish C1, immediate two-bar colour success is about 47.36% of original opportunities, while waiting success is about 30.03%; conditioning on confirmation hides missed opportunities.
Ordinary controls can include older run ages; the later age-two diagnostic is exploratory. Costs, fills and exact completion remain unresolved, and Study 08 shares the underlying history.

assessments.blocker: Conditional colour lift does not overcome negative price proxies or establish a like-for-like executable waiting-policy gain.

assessments.rationale: The session overlay does not rescue the failed price candidates. Colour-only segment standouts remain exploratory, depend on shared source histories and cannot be pooled into a trade edge.

Return-first, extension-first, neither and ambiguous all remain in the denominator; unequal target distances make a 50% winner benchmark invalid.

assessments.scope: The unfiltered GC outer-lower-band long candidate at the displayed ten-bar cooldown and twenty-bar horizon; other grid cells are sensitivities.
assessments.rationale: The excursion study documents path scale but no stable material long advantage. Later adverse movement is substantial and terminal movement remains uncertain; selecting a favorable MFE would invent an exit.
assessments.materiality: At the fixed default, 2026 YTD mean MAE/MFE is 30.94/23.91 GC points on 245 complete paths; mean terminal move is −0.15 points (95% −5.15 to 4.86). Separate extrema cannot be subtracted into realized P&L.

supporting.text: 2025 default terminal mean is +1.75 GC points on 207 valid paths, but its interval includes zero; this supplies limited, uncertain support for a bounce question.

contrary.text: The 2026 default mean adverse excursion exceeds favorable excursion; the GC-point scale is far larger than 2025 and should not be pooled into a fixed risk rule.
The 2026 default terminal mean is slightly negative with a wide interval despite a terminal-positive rate above half.
The parameter grid is exploratory and dependent; adjusted history and eligibility are retrospective, and stops, ordering, fills, slippage and net profitability are untested.

assessments.blocker: There is no fixed executable exit or time-matched price baseline showing positive after-cost advantage; excursion maxima are unattainable hindsight exits.

nextTest.description: Only reopen after freezing a single exit policy at this same default, with finer paths for sequencing and unadjusted fills/costs, versus a time/volatility-matched GC baseline on genuinely later dates.

nextTest.rejects: Reject if the bounce remains terminally uncertain or negative after costs, or apparent profit requires choosing exits from observed MAE/MFE.

assessments.scope: The frozen upper-half-close filter selected in 2025 for GC lower-band longs, applied unchanged to the ten-bar cooldown/twenty-bar horizon chronological 2026 check.
assessments.rationale: The simple causal filter improves the descriptive risk score directionally in both years, warranting a discriminating test. The 2026 interval spans zero, its score stays negative, and that year was previously viewed.
assessments.materiality: The 2026 capped MFE-minus-MAE score improves by 0.131 signal sigma, from −0.309 to −0.179, with 182 filtered versus 245 baseline paths. This path-selection score is not realized return; materiality requires incremental net GC ticks under one executable policy.

supporting.text: The selected upper-half-close rule improved the 2025 score by 0.263 sigma and the unchanged 2026 score by 0.131 sigma, retaining the declared signal-time condition.

contrary.text: The 2026 score-difference interval is about −0.047 to +0.316 sigma, including no improvement, and the filtered score remains negative.

2026 unfiltered outcomes were already viewed in Study 12. Nine-filter selection, correlated sensitivities, retrospective adjusted history and absent stop/target ordering or costs prevent protected-validation or profitability claims.

assessments.scope: Original NQ Asia A–C research; the narrow follow-up candidate is short setup B, a developing value-boundary breakout/retest. Later D/E extensions are excluded from this public assessment.
assessments.rationale: The short B retest has a specific matched favorable-excursion advantage worth defining as a trade policy. The original POC and HVN alternatives are inconclusive or adverse, and the B result has no saved costed payoff or terminal-return advantage. More MFE is an opportunity envelope, not capturable profit; this supports definition and testing rather than an execution claim.
assessments.materiality: Use incremental net NQ points per filled short B setup and per eligible Asia session against the saved same-year/side/hour/volatility-matched control. The saved +2.76-point MFE contrast is not net expectancy. A future protocol should require a predeclared economically useful net hurdle, for example one NQ point per fill after spread, fees and slippage, with participation and risk reported.

supporting.text: The original 2024–2025 short B 30-minute comparison saves matched MFE +2.7588 NQ points, 95% interval [0.6428, 5.1007], across 540 complete matched events. This is a specific path difference against matched controls.

contrary.text: POC reversal remains inconclusive and short HVN fades show worse adverse excursion; these do not corroborate a universal Asia-level edge.

Profiles approximate bar volume; prior inspection, retrospective completeness, unresolved intrabar fills and absent independent execution/profile parity remain material limits. No costed stop/target policy is demonstrated.

assessments.blocker: A favorable-excursion difference has not been converted into causal, costed entry/exit expectancy; the validation history was previously inspected and the complete primary family does not support a general level strategy.

nextTest.description: Freeze only short B with one causal next-open entry, one stop/exit and a same-hour/volatility comparator, then evaluate genuinely new NQ history using original profile settings and conservative fills. Preserve all eligible sessions and missing outcomes; test the complete declared cost scenario.
nextTest.supports: Net points per fill exceed the frozen material hurdle with a week-clustered lower uncertainty bound above zero, positive incremental session expectancy, and no dependence on optimistic fill order.
nextTest.rejects: Net advantage is nonpositive, below the material hurdle, erased by realistic friction, or not reproducible from levels known before the touch.

assessments.scope: Price-only VWAP excursion/response research across ES/NQ/GC and four anchors. The proposed discriminating candidate is GC Globex 2σ departure continuation over 10 two-minute candles, not a universal VWAP fade.
assessments.rationale: Most equity-index directional means are inconclusive, while GC has modest positive 20-minute continuation means at several overlapping anchors. The Globex result is narrow enough to specify a test but small in outright price units and unsupported by saved execution, costs or a matched entry benchmark. Anchors and nested thresholds cannot be counted as replications.
assessments.materiality: Judge net GC points per eligible continuation and incremental net points versus a same-anchor/time baseline, including genuine no-trades. The saved Globex mean is only +0.18 gross points over 20 minutes; a future materiality gate such as at least one native GC tick (0.1 point) incremental net expectancy must survive fully specified spread, commission and slippage.

supporting.text: At the primary 2σ departure and 20-minute horizon, GC Globex continuation has saved mean +0.18 points, 95% interval [0.04, 0.33], N=3,793. GC Asia/NY are also positive descriptively, with overlapping histories.

contrary.text: GC London continuation is near zero and most ES/NQ signed means include zero; return/touch frequencies do not establish a profitable fade.

Whole-day eligibility is retrospective; anchors overlap, thresholds nest and intervals are marginal. OHLC touches, missing paths and double-barrier ambiguity do not establish fills or net profitability.

assessments.blocker: No frozen executable trade policy, cost model or matched causal baseline exists, and the observed gross GC mean is small enough for ordinary friction to matter.

nextTest.supports: Incremental net expectancy clears the predeclared 0.1-point material gate with a week-clustered lower bound above zero and remains positive under adverse fill sensitivity.
nextTest.rejects: The small gross mean disappears after costs, fails against the comparator, is unstable across new calendar blocks, or depends on retrospective eligibility.
